page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable virtual server built on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz, the instance presents 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Memory allocation includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance features CPU flags including AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction set extensions. It operates without dedicated local NVMe storage and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the t3a.xlarge exhibits modest compute and memory throughput reflecting its burstable architecture. Single-core stress-ng tests recorded 566.4 while multi-core yielded 1181.97, placing CPU execution performance in the lower tier. Memory read bandwidth reached 23.87 GB/sec for large uncached blocks with a write bandwidth of 11.7 GB/sec. The instance scored 3622.97 in Passmark CPU tests, though its Passmark encryption test achieved an average score of 3207.35. Network and service workloads produced 2.53 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.73 GB/sec throughput for static web serving.

Given its burstable CPU model and standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the t3a.xlarge delivers cost-effective resource density for workloads with fluctuating compute requirements. By relying on CPU credits rather than sustained high-frequency compute, it minimizes baseline operational costs. The provision of 16 GB DDR4 RAM accommodates application runtimes, code staging environments, and low-traffic web applications, though continuous peak multi-core processing will exhaust CPU credits and limit overall performance. Suitable deployments include non-critical build servers, staging instances, microservices, and light database caching.
description: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable virtual server powered by a 2.2 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 processor based on x86_64 architecture and managed by the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs over 2 physical cores, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 system memory at 3 GHz, delivering a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio without attached local storage. Benchmark results place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in low performance tiers, though hardware-accelerated crypto functions such as AES and SHA_NI deliver average Passmark encryption performance. Baseline network bandwidth is configured at 1 Gbps. Due to its burstable baseline CPU model, the t3a.xlarge provides cost-efficient hosting for workloads with variable utilization profiles, such as internal development environments, light web servers, background task workers, and staging systems that do not require continuous sustained compute capacity.
